One deal, nine people, two worlds

Northwind Logistics Platform subscription $180,000 a year · five-year term Close date 30 September 15 changes returned on their own paper

All names and figures invented.

Review is the engine we already sell. Two new decisions sit around it, and two things get added to what it shows. Scope, before Review: what does this need. Review, ours today: what to redline, with reasoning, and what sits above the limit. Added to it: a price on each change, meaning what this change is worth in this deal. Commitments, after signature: what we owe, and what would break it. The second addition to Review is the cost of each position: not what one change is worth here, but what holding that same position has cost across every deal, once there are quarters of outcomes behind it. That one ships last, so the prices shown below are all deal-side. The CRM pull, the promise check, the conflict check and the authority limit are not engines: they are retrieval, comparison and a written rule.

Review MIND

Three need your judgment. Eleven are inside standard. One is outside your authority. This is Review as it works today.

Ranked and flagged exactly as Review does now. What is new is the price on each change, where the term has one. The 3% uplift is worth $55,600 over five years. A liability cap has no price until something goes wrong.

Added to Review · the cost of a position

Put the 3% back, or trade it against the extra discount they asked for in 4.1.

Review already proposes the counter. The addition is how often that position has held and what it cost, which needs quarters of outcomes. Ships last. Shown here so the walkthrough reflects the finished thing.

What Priya still decides

Every one. It proposes and shows its working. Nothing reaches Northwind until she sends it, which is also why she is the merge point: finance and security land their positions on this screen, and anything linked arrives together rather than as separate items.

Why this is expensive

One question. Clause 6.3.

They changed payment from net 30 on signing to milestones on acceptance. The only change that touches you. The other fourteen do not. It is linked to clause 14, termination, which Priya is reviewing now: if you reject the milestone structure, her termination position changes too.

Quoted in full, with our standard version alongside. He never opens the forty pages.

Answers in four minutes, on day one, before anyone negotiates around it. Priya sees his answer land against clause 14 before she commits her own.

Day 19

Her conclusion

Their changes do not touch the security schedule and they hold no customer data. Nothing to do.

The cost

Thirteen days to establish there was nothing to establish. Nothing could go back to Northwind until it cleared, and nobody could tell Dana when that would be.
Nadia's queue · day 1

Northwind is not in it

Not asked, and that is correct. The four that do need her are in the queue instead, each with the specific concern named.

Scope MIND · why you were skipped

Visible to Nadia, and challengeable.

Their markup does not touch the security schedule, the data terms, or what data they hold. Every skip is logged with its reasoning, and she can disagree with any of them.

An overruled skip is not a bug report. It is how it learns.

Nadia keeps the veto

Security will never accept being skipped by something they cannot inspect. Being left out is only acceptable while the reasoning is visible and she can overrule it.

Rafael's inbox

Review MIND · above the limit

Clause 12: indemnity extended to their end customers.

Our standard position, why it is above the limit, the three times we granted it in four years and the cap each time, and what we are inclined to do.

What the framing changes

Rafael bills for judgment instead of for rebuilding context. Sending the question rather than the document is where outside-counsel spend falls, off the same asset as everything else here: knowing what we did before.

Elena · same request, one page in front of it

Review MIND · what is nonstandard

One term out of fifteen changes.

Clause 12 extends indemnity to their end customers. Above standard. Approved by the Deputy GC, capped at twice annual fees, in line with the three previous times.

Everything else is standard.

What changes

She still signs in a minute. She now knows what she signed.
Sam, eleven months later

Incident channel

Northwind has escalated. Their contract promises a four-hour P1 response, not next business day. Nobody had heard this. It was agreed in a negotiation Sam never saw.

And the other direction

Last month his team shipped a feature adding an AI vendor that handles customer data. Several signed agreements require notice first. Nobody checked, because checking meant reading two hundred contracts.

Commitments MIND · outward

You now owe Northwind a four-hour P1 response.

Agreed 3 October, nonstandard, owner assigned to your on-call rotation. In your tracker the day it was signed, not eleven months later in an incident.

Commitments MIND · inward

This release adds a subprocessor. Fourteen agreements require notice first.

The new AI vendor will handle customer data on our behalf, which makes it a subprocessor under the data terms in those fourteen contracts. Each one requires notice before we add it, and gives the other side a window to object. In two of them, an unresolved objection lets them end the affected services. Raised in the release checklist before deploy, and escalated to Priya with the list.

Where Sam sits

Never in the negotiation, on both ends of it. Going out, a signature triggers it. Coming in, a deploy does.
Tomás · counsel at Northwind

His own Outlook, his own Word

Contract arrives as an attachment. He marks it up in Word. He emails it back. He waits. A response arrives. He marks it up again.
Tomás · counsel at Northwind

His own Outlook, his own Word

Contract arrives as an attachment. He marks it up in Word. He emails it back. He waits, less. A response arrives. He marks it up again.

No MIND reaches him

That is the design, not a limitation.

He will never log into our system or learn our interface. Any design that needs him to is a design that does not ship. He only notices that responses arrive faster and contradict each other less.

Everything here is invented: the customer, the deal, the clause numbers, the people. Priya sends every response. Deal desk and sales leadership are absent on purpose: this markup does not touch pricing, and their view is the forecast rather than the contract.
